blurb: A prototype of Matthew's tree-streams for Hazel's Checkers search: one tree of boards both players grow, answers kept as ranges and found by a partial order. When the two players' searches end on the same move, the one that comes second does about half the work; lining them up costs one player a move of look-ahead, and black 6 with white 5 runs 63% faster than Hazel now. Keeping the tree itself halves the moves worked out but saves no time in JavaScript, and deepening a step at a time saves nothing here.
title: One Search Tree for Two Players
